nina: Quick heads-up — noticed a latency bump for short-seq traffic (seq<=32) in us-west after the kernel selector tweak last night.
rob: Which selector tweak exactly? The one that prefers fused-gemm on Ampere?
nina: Yeah — we biased selector to pick the fused path when batch>1. Good for long sequences but seems to add launch overhead for small seqs.
angela: Do we have traces/prof samples or just metrics?
perf-bot: Attached perf summary (sampled timeline):
```
seq=16, batch=1  -> launch=180us exec=120us  total~300us
seq=16, batch=4  -> launch=210us exec=480us  total~690us
seq=128, batch=8 -> launch=200us exec=2400us total~2600us
```
liam: Launch is non-negligible at short seqs. If launch_cost ~= per-request overhead, fused kernel wins for throughput but hurts p99 on tiny requests.
rob: Sounds like our autotuner objective (throughput-focused) missed latency for short seqs. We should include a seq-dependent penalty.
angela: Also note KV cache behavior: cold-client pattern causes extra kernel invocations for warmup which amplifies launch costs.
nina: Yup — KV miss path bounces between smaller kernels and triggers the batcher to merge heterogeneous seqs, which then pushes fused picks. Bad combo.
liam: Proposal: model cost as launch_cost + per_token_cost * seq. Evaluate per-kernel on that metric and pick min. That makes threshold explicit.
rob: Agree. Also add a small hysteresis so we don't thrash between kernels when batch composition fluctuates.
angela: Can we also bias scheduler to coalesce requests by preferred-kernel tag? Grouping same-kernel requests reduces relative launch overhead.
ina: We tried a kernel-tagging pilot last month — improved amortization but increased tail for multi-tenant mixes. Might need tenant-aware grouping.
liam: For quick mitigation, revert fused preference for (batch<=2 && seq<=64) or force low-launch kernel for those cases.
ina: I'll run a microbench matrix today: seq in [8,16,32,64,128], batch in [1,2,4,8], kernels=[fused,winograd,cuBLAS], KV=[warm,cold], continuous_batching=[on,off]. Will post results.
rob: Add `batcher.conf` toggles and `selector` telemetry to the runs so autotuner sees decision context.
perf-bot: Regression alert: p99 +18% for short sequences in us-west, triggered 03:12 UTC.
angela: Please file an incident note so SRE/support can triage customer impact.
liam: Also track cost delta — fused path may be slightly cheaper per-token but not if it raises tail for API customers.
nina: Filed INC-2026-104 in incidents channel and started the bench jobs. Will share raw traces + autotune logs in ~2h. :thumbsup:
rob: Thanks — if the bench shows clear cut points we can teach selector a simple rule before changing objective function.
angela: One more ask: include KV hit-rate histogram in the report. It's key to reproduce the warm/cold amplification.
nina: Will include KV hist and a small flamegraph snippet.
liam: Nice. Ping me when results are up, I'll prototype the cost formula.
nina: Will do.
